rv.q: Performed using the Olivier's in the round configuration, this production is stripped back and stark — the unadorned approach makes you newly receptive.
It is a burning nugget of recent history... It hasn't lost its heat at all – it's white-hot, forever.
But its power endures: tough, tender and devastating.
Kramer's play is living history, written without the benefit of hindsight, and it remains undimmed by time.
Dominic Cooke's revival is reverential and disconcertingly drab, the actors marooned on Vicki Mortimer's stark, in-the-round set.

The Normal Heart covers the years 1981–84 and, when I first saw it at the Theatre in 1986, it still felt like a dispatch from the front. Today, though HIV is no longer an automatic death sentence, the play has lost none of its anger and its power to be moving.
